note: Rewritten from entry 53 (pp. 364–366) in Roonwal and Chhotani (1997), the original in English; three castes are recorded, the alate, the soldier and the pseudoworker, the pseudoworker being merged into the "Worker" section. The synonymy list, literature citations, figure numbers, type specimens and distribution information of the original have not been entered. Doubtful OCR readings (e.g. "vaieriae", "vakriae") have been read as valeriae following the entry name.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Alate with head capsule, postclypeus, wing scales and abdomen pale chestnut brown, the frontal area darker; body length (excluding wings) about 5.9 mm, head length (to the mandibular base) and head width including the compound eyes both 1.0 mm. Soldier head capsule nearly rectangular (head length to mandibular base 1.48–1.57 mm, width 1.20–1.28 mm), with two bluntly pointed horn-like processes projecting from the anterolateral parts of the head — one near the anterolateral margin of the postclypeus, the other an extension of the ventral gena — which is the key character separating this species from the other Indian species of the genus; body length about 4.95–6.44 mm; left mandible with 4 marginal teeth, right mandible with 2 marginal teeth in the middle.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule, postclypeus, wing scales and abdomen pale chestnut brown, the head darker in the frontal area; ocelli and anteclypeus transparent; labrum yellowish brown; antennae brown with pale yellow tips. Head and body sparsely hairy. Body length (excluding wings) about 5.9 mm. Head capsule nearly rectangular-oval, widest at the compound eyes (head length to mandibular base and head width including compound eyes both 1.0 mm); a little hair scattered all over; frons slightly inclined towards the clypeus; Y-shaped suture faintly visible. Compound eyes large, black, nearly circular (maximum diameter 0.30 mm, minimum diameter 0.24 mm), close to the antennae. Ocelli nearly oval (maximum diameter 0.10 mm), translucent, close to the compound eyes (eye-ocellus distance 0.02 mm). Antennae with more than 9 segments, segments 3 and 5 subequal and shortest. Anteclypeus hairless, trapezoidal, anterior margin straight. Postclypeus flat, narrow, indistinctly separated from the frons, with a few short hairs at the anterior corners. Labrum broadly ligulate (length 0.23 mm, width 0.40 mm), sides converging to an almost straight anterior margin. Pronotum shield-shaped, nearly rectangular (length 0.73 mm, width 1.04 mm), wider than the head width including compound eyes; margins and surface with a few hairs. Legs short and stout, tibial apical spur formula 3:3:3. Abdomen long-oval; cerci 2-segmented, 0.05 mm long; styli single-segmented, 0.06 mm long.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Anterior part of the head capsule, postclypeus and mandibles dark chestnut brown; the rest of the head, the antennae and the thorax reddish brown; legs and abdomen yellowish brown. Head and body rather densely hairy. Body length about 4.95–6.44 mm. Head capsule nearly rectangular (head length to mandibular base 1.48–1.57 mm, width 1.20–1.28 mm), the middle of the frons depressed and sloping forwards at 45°; two bluntly pointed horn-like processes project from the anterolateral parts of the head behind the antennae, one near the anterolateral margin of the postclypeus and the other an extension of the ventral gena. Compound eyes translucent, nearly oval (maximum diameter 0.15–0.18 mm, minimum diameter 0.10–0.13 mm), their distance from the antennae slightly less than their minimum diameter; ocelli absent. Antennae 11–13-segmented, segment 4 shortest. Anteclypeus band-like, transparent, hairless; postclypeus trapezoidal, with a few hairs on the anterior margin. Labrum short and wide, slightly pointed in front, with a tuft of hairs at the apex. Mandibles stout and large, strongly incurved at the apex, the teeth stout; left mandible with 4 marginal teeth, right mandible with 2 marginal teeth in the middle. Postmentum short, club-shaped, widest slightly below the middle, the waist width about half the maximum width (length 0.75–0.84 mm, maximum width 0.38–0.40 mm, waist width 0.20 mm). Pronotum flat, semicircular, anterior margin deeply concave, sides rounded, posterior margin nearly straight, as wide as the head (length 0.70–0.75 mm, width 1.20–1.28 mm). Legs of moderate length, hairy, tibial apical spur formula 3:3:3. Abdomen long, hairy; cerci 2-segmented, 0.08–0.13 mm long; styli single-segmented, 0.05–0.08 mm long.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Called pseudoworker in the original. Head capsule and body pale milky white, postclypeus and labrum pale yellow, mandibular teeth dark brown. Rather densely hairy. Body length 4.8–6.6 mm. Head capsule nearly circular (head length to mandibular base 1.05–1.10 mm). Compound eyes reduced, oval, colourless, appearing as spots. Antennae 13-segmented, segments 4 and 5 subequal and shortest. Anteclypeus band-like, transparent, hairless; postclypeus trapezoidal, with a row of long hairs at its base. Labrum wide, ligulate. Pronotum wider than long (length 0.60–0.70 mm, width 1.08–1.10 mm), semicircular, hairy; anterior margin concave, posterior margin nearly straight.
